speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Over the past six decades, it has institutionalised the rights and responsibilities of men and women in marriage and ensured the welfare and protection of women in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: And, for divorce, our first priority is to save marriages, but where divorce is inevitable, we must foster therapeutic justice to bring about healing so that the family can move on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We strive to reduce acrimony and ensure child-centricity in the proceedings, including parental responsibility and cooperative co-parenting post-divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, we recognise that we can do more to strengthen the institution of marriage and safeguard the welfare of children in the event of divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have engaged citizens and stakeholders extensively on the divorce process, especially on the proposed divorce by mutual agreement of the irretrievable breakdown of marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We started this since 2020, when we convened a Citizen Panel involving more than 150 divorcees over a four-month period, many of whom bravely shared their marriage and divorce experiences with us, so that we can understand what they went through and make the necessary changes in our law and policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also engaged social work practitioners, community and religious leaders, and law practitioners, academics and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Furthermore, as part of the year-long, nationwide Conversations on Singapore's Women’s Development last year, as well as through the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships that I lead, our citizens and other stakeholders have given us feedback on strengthening marriages and supporting families undergoing divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Having reviewed this feedback, we propose to: one, enhance the marriage process and strengthen safeguards to protect the institution of marriage; two, strengthen therapeutic justice in the divorce process and ensure those affected by divorce are supported; and three, ensure the Women's Charter remains up to date.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The first category of proposals aims to enhance the marriage process to provide convenience to couples looking to start on their marriage journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These changes are in line with the digital transformation of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: And we are also looking to update the necessary safeguards to ensure that the institution of marriage is not abused.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, to marry under the Women's Charter, most steps, from pre-solemnisation to solemnisation, must be completed in-person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has demonstrated that there are circumstances in which this may be difficult.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Certain aspects of the process, such as the verification of documents, can also be digitalised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Changes to the current marriage process include, first, the repeal of the existing section 17 by clause 10.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the existing section 17, parties who intend to marry must submit a statutory declaration of certain matters, for example, that the parties are not prevented by law from marrying.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A statutory declaration must be made in person before a Commissioner for Oaths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With the repeal of section 17, instead of a statutory declaration, parties will only make a declaration in the prescribed form online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The contents of the declaration and the consequences of a false declaration will be similar to that for the statutory declaration required today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clause 19 repeals the current section 31, which requires signed and sealed copies of hard copy marriage certificates to be issued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The new section 30 will no longer require hard copy certificates, and digital certificates will be issued instead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This was first introduced during the circuit breaker in May 2020 as a temporary option under the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) for Solemnisation and Registration of Marriages Act 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clause 43 will repeal this Act and clause 15 will make this a permanent option under the Women's Charter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, couples may still hold their solemnisations in-person and, indeed, most couples prefer this option as the solemnisation is a significant and momentous occasion and couples often wish to celebrate with their loved ones in-person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As a safeguard, where there are concerns, such as an individual lacking mental capacity or marriages of convenience, the couple may not perform the declaration online or the Registrar of Marriages may decide not to permit any couple to solemnise their marriage via video-link.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The marriage process is significant and should continue to reflect the solemnity of the marriage contract.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Hence, we will continue to provide couples with a ceremonial marriage certificate for keepsake.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise the important roles solemnisers play in the marriage journey of couples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We launched the one-year pilot in December 2021 with 20 selected solemnisers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Through this, we aim to create a Community of Practice for licensed solemnisers to share best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Many couples also complete pre-marital counselling courses with their religious organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Through the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships, religious organisations are stepping forward to do more to prepare young couples for marriage and to mentor them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Another set of marriage-related proposals involves updating safeguards to ensure that the institution of marriage is not abused.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We want to ensure that the Registry of Marriages can continue to perform due diligence in all applications for marriage by satisfying itself that parties have the capacity to marry and are entering into a marriage willingly and in good faith.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, non-residents who are not Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents, including those with no nexus to Singapore, can marry here, as long as at least one party has been present in Singapore for 15 days preceding the filing of the Notice of Marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We do not want to become a marriage hub for marriages where neither party has any nexus to Singapore, as it could compromise ROM's ability to carry out its due diligence and, inadvertently, undermine the significance of marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This would prevent couples, where both parties are on Short-Term Visit Passes which are valid for up to 30 days, from marrying here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, for exceptional cases, the Registrar will be empowered to waive this requirement should he or she be satisfied that there is good reason to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also want to restrict the persons who can obtain information from the State Marriage Register.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clauses 18 and 19 will amend the existing section 27 and existing section 180 of the Women's Charter, to allow the Minister to make rules on the provision of copies or extracts from the Register.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Information from the Register contains personal particulars of the parties, including their NRIC numbers, and we wish to prevent the misuse of such information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Separately, individuals will still retain two free online searches within a 12-month period, or may opt for a paid search, to enquire whether a person is married.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These searches will show if there is a marriage record for the party in question and the date of marriage, with the name and NRIC of the spouse redacted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This search function will remain available to all and is not limited only to couples intending to marry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Next, clause 15 will repeal the existing section 24 and replace it with a new section 23, to allow religious ceremonies to be conducted before, on or after solemnisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Unlike when the Women's Charter was first enacted, the general public is now aware that parties must go through the solemnisation process to be married in the eyes of the law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Registry of Marriages has also received appeals to allow the religious ceremony to take place before or during the solemnisation and, so, we wish to remove unnecessary restrictions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Lastly, clause 40 repeals and re-enacts the existing section 180A to introduce new safeguards for licensed solemnisers by according them protection from personal liability if they had acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now move on to the next category of proposals, which pertains to divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These proposals seek to amend the law on divorce in line with the aims of therapeutic justice in the divorce process and enhance support for those undergoing divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In November 2017, MSF, MinLaw and FJC formed the Committee to Review and Enhance Reforms in the Family Justice System, or the RERF Committee, in short.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The RERF Committee made its recommendations, aimed at further strengthening the family justice system and submitted its report in September 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The RERF's aspiration was the adoption of therapeutic justice in the family justice system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the context of family justice and couples undergoing divorce, therapeutic justice is a "lens of care" that seeks to help distressed families move forward in a more positive way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It seeks not to position parties as adversaries in Court, but as problem-solvers, collaborating to seek solutions that will facilitate healing, restoration and the recasting of a move that is positive in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are proposing to effect these recommendations through the Women's Charter amendments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, under the Women's Charter, divorcing parties must prove the sole ground for divorce, which is the "irretrievable breakdown of the marriage" before a divorce is granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To do this, they may cite one or more of the existing five facts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There are three fault-based facts of adultery, desertion and unreasonable behaviour, and two non-fault facts of separation of three years with consent and of four years without.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To better understand how to incorporate therapeutic justice in the divorce process, we engaged more than 150 divorcees and other stakeholders closely involved and acquainted with the divorce process on their experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Jane, which is not her real name, shared the pain that she went through during her divorce three years ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Initially, she and her ex-husband had wanted to settle their divorce amicably.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, they had to pinpoint each other's faults to prove that their marriage had broken down irretrievably and this led to many quarrels and worsened their relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: While Jane admitted that there were faults on both sides, she wished there was an option to allow them to acknowledge they were jointly responsible rather than blame each other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In fact, in our engagements with social service practitioners and several religious organisations, they had also shared that they had worked in earnest and as best as they could with couples, but there were instances where the couples were just unable to reconcile.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In such cases, where there are children involved in the marriage, the marriage is no longer a matter just between the couple.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Children are innocent parties involved in an unfortunate situation, and we must try as much as possible to minimise their exposure to the pain and conflict that often accompany divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, with the current divorce regime, we have found that where parties agree on the divorce, having to cite one of the existing facts may force parties to point fingers at each other as they cite reasons to prove one of the three fault-based facts or dredge up past hurts to prove the facts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This can cause the child to be caught in the middle as allegations of misdeeds are being made by either or both of their parents against the other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If parties were to cite separation as a fact so as to avoid blaming each other, they have to put their lives on hold for three to four years, which can be harmful to the couple and their children as the relationship between the couple would likely be tense and unstable during the period of separation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This aims to reduce acrimony in divorce and better allow the family to heal and move on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Irretrievable breakdown of the marriage will remain the sole ground for divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Subsection (6)(b) also states that the Court must consider the stated matters in deciding whether to order further mediation, counselling or family support programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This may happen if the Court finds the required submission is insufficient or believes there is a possibility of reconciliation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We, therefore, envisage that the key aspects of divorce by mutual agreement to be: (a) joint responsibility, where unlike fault-based facts, parties may cite reasons where they take joint responsibility for the breakdown of their marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, they may cite deep-seated differences in values.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: (b) reconciliation, as efforts to reconcile are explicitly required and the Court can order interventions and must reject any agreement if it concludes that reconciliation is reasonably possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: (c) joint consideration of post-divorce arrangements to set parties into the right frame to jointly consider their children and financial affairs so as to reduce tension at the ancillary matters stage, where the issues of the children, division of matrimonial assets and maintenance are discussed and better ensure positive outcomes post-divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now elaborate more on the test under divorce by mutual agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: First, parties must agree that their marriage has broken down irretrievably and explain the reasons leading them to conclude this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They must state attempts they have made at reconciliation and they must state considerations they have given to the arrangements to be made for their financial affairs and children post-divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A bare agreement without reasons is not enough.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Also, as with agreements in other contexts, parties must be acting voluntarily, have the requisite knowledge of the terms and intend to enter into the agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Second, beyond what generally constitutes an agreement in other contexts, the Court will reject the agreement if there remains a reasonable possibility that parties might reconcile.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is a parties-centric test, assessed based on the circumstances of each individual case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The reasons given by parties will inform the assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For instance, in cases where previous efforts at reconciliation were few and insufficient, where reasons provided on the breakdown of the marriage appear vague and arbitrary and where parties do not seem entirely certain of their decision, the Court may choose not to accept the agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The sufficiency or otherwise of the parties' reasons will inform the Court's assessment as to whether there remains a reasonable possibility of reconciliation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Whether there is such a possibility is a factual question in each case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As a parties-centric test, the possibility of reconciliation does not require the Court to impose an external, objective test for whether the marriage has broken down.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: At the same time, it permits the Court to weed out sham or frivolous agreements or cases where the parties are seeking a divorce for collateral reasons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We leave it to the Court to apply the test in actual cases and to develop the case law in this area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If the Court believes there is a reasonable possibility of reconciliation, it can send the parties for mediation, counselling and family support programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In some cases, this might salvage the marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In other cases, this would confirm there truly is no longer a reasonable possibility of reconciliation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There may be concerns that parties who wish to rely on divorce by mutual agreement (DMA) may request their lawyers to frame the Court documents in a manner that suggests that they have tried their best to reconcile, although this may not be true.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Divorce lawyers must, therefore, continue to behave ethically, provide proper advice in line with the principles of therapeutic justice and continue to uphold their duties as officers of the Court and to assist in the administration of justice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A fundamental mindset shift is necessary within the divorce process, where parties are not positioned as adversaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They are part of a family unit and, while they have ended their marriage, they will always be family to their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The focus should be on promoting healing and transitioning into the next phase with dignity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: All involved in the divorce process must embrace this mindset shift, especially divorce lawyers, who are, often, closest to the parties in the process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: More must be done to foster healing in the relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Therefore, we are exploring amending terms, such as "defendant" and "plaintiff", to less adversarial terms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are considering the feasibility of amending these terms under separate legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The sole ground of divorce remains, which is, the irretrievable breakdown of marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Court also retains the power to refuse to grant a divorce if it would not be just and reasonable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Second, within the DMA framework itself, there are safeguards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Court has the power to order parties to attend mediation, counselling and family support programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This will help filter out cases where reconciliation is still reasonably possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I should also point out that entering into a marriage of convenience is an offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Thus, given the safeguards, parties to a sham marriage will find it difficult to obtain a divorce through DMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There may be concerns that a vulnerable spouse may be coerced into agreeing to divorce under DMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is not a new concern or one specific to DMA as a vulnerable spouse could, today, already be coerced into agreeing to the divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We rely, primarily, on family lawyers to prevent such cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, the Mandatory Parenting Programme, or MPP, which is a mandatory pre-filing programme for parents that I will elaborate on later, can act as a safeguard against this as the counsellor may identify and assist such spouses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I would also like to point out that DMA does not absolve either party from their responsibilities in providing maintenance to their child or spouse if the Court makes such an order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I would also like to highlight that DMA is different from the type of "no-fault" divorce in other jurisdictions where parties are not required to take responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Unlike in other jurisdictions, DMA will require parties to state the reasons that have led them to conclude that their marriage has irretrievably broken down.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In doing so, parties would have to jointly take responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now move on to the other divorce-related proposals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For parents in the process of a divorce, we want to support them in co-parenting effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, where a party with minor children files for divorce on the standard track, that is, without having reached an agreement with his/her spouse on the reason for divorce or ancillary matters, he or she must attend MPP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The same applies to a party who has been served with divorce papers on the standard track and wishes to file a counterclaim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, parties who agree on the divorce and all ancillary matters and, thus, file for divorce on the simplified divorce track, do not, currently, need to attend MPP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MPP encourages parents to make informed decisions that prioritise the well-being of their children and helps parents understand the importance of co-parenting and the practical issues arising from a divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MPP will be enhanced to focus more on co-parenting and provide personalised information for parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This would include self-assessments and information on where to seek timely support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that there may be other caregivers involved in the child's life, such as grandparents, and clause 38 introduces a new section 139I to empower the Court to advise that such key related persons participate in necessary programmes as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF remains committed to saving marriages where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For couples who decide to work on their marriage while attending MPP, they could choose to attend marital counselling services provided by FAM@FSC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If couples are of the same faith and are open to marital counselling provided by religious organisations, they may opt for counselling provided by such organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will work with interested religious organisations which wish to be involved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: She remembers standing outside a lawyer's office as her mother told her to tell her father that he will never see her again if he does not turn up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: At the young age of eight, she was often made the middle person, passing messages between her parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: She felt distressed and unsafe, yet was afraid to reach out for help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: She emphasised the need to better support children of divorced parents through counselling and check-ins to address these problems early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, MSF has the Children-in-Between Programme to support parents and children impacted by divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is a group programme comprising parental and child components.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Programme for Children emphasises and encompasses a range of possible support for children, including an assessment of the needs of the child and specific interventions, such as group programmes, counselling or psychological services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The assessment would be used to make recommendations to parents on suitable interventions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Interventions of varying intensity will be available to address the differing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If the Court's advice is not complied with, the Court will have the discretion to make any order as it deems fit and, in relevant cases, may take the non-compliance of the parents into consideration in making custody, care and control and access orders, among other relevant factors, in determining the welfare of the child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Next, I will share our proposals to enhance the child access order enforcement regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, where there is non-compliance with a child access order, the only recourse for the access parent is to commence committal proceedings or apply for care and control orders pertaining to the child to be varied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, this can be a difficult and time-consuming process and it may be some time before the access parent is able to gain access.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Therefore, clause 35 enacts section 126B to provide a range of measures for the enforcement of child access orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We understand that there are divorced parents who struggle to gain access to their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We sympathise with this and trust that these new measures will go somewhat to help address this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, we would like to reiterate that, in such issues, it is in the child's best interest for parents to resolve these issues through effective communication and mutual understanding and legal measures should be a last resort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Lastly, for the divorce-related proposals, I will share our proposals to enhance the maintenance enforcement regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are considering the feasibility of taking these up under other legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This includes adopting an inquisitorial approach in hearing enforcement applications, streamlining procedures and strengthening deterrence against non-payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Beyond legal and procedural reforms, we will also continue to link those that cannot pay to support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now move on to the amendments to update the more archaic portions of the Women's Charter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Part 6 of the Women's Charter, currently, sets out the specific rights of a married woman, such as the right to hold and dispose of property, and states that she is liable for her own debts, contracts and wrongs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These specific rights reflect the historical development of married women's rights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the old common law, women ceased to have any independent legal personality upon marriage and, therefore, could not make contracts and hold property and so on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the UK, this began to change in the late 1800s, with law reforms that gave married women the same rights as married men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The provisions in Part 6 can be traced back to these law reforms, which were made incrementally over many years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Separately, we are also taking the opportunity to completely abolish some archaic concepts in this area of the law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government is committed to building an inclusive and fair society where every Singaporean, both men and women, have full and equal opportunities to contribute to our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Singapore women have made tremendous progress since our Independence in 1965.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our women's standing in society has risen steadily, attaining higher education levels which are on par with men, and more women are participating in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This move to update the Women's Charter is also symbolic of how far we have come in terms of women's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Even as we recognise the significant progress made, we can continue do more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Feedback from the Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development shows that deep-seated attitudes and mindsets about gender stereotypes persist and the belief and aspirations for marriage and families remain strong.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government will continue to empower, protect and uplift our women in the workplace and in their caregiving roles and, especially, in protecting them from harm and violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The amendments we have proposed attempt to: first, make the marriage process more couple-centric and update the safeguards; two, strengthen the divorce process by incorporating therapeutic justice into the process and ensuring those impacted by the divorce are supported; three, update the provisions and terminology in the Women’s Charter to abolish archaic concepts that no longer reflect the progress of women today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Government efforts and legislative levers can only go so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We must work together as a society to effect change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships will harness ground-up initiatives and galvanise a whole-of-society response to ensure that strong families remain as the basic building block of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: That is to say, the amendments play little part in telling the parties what the decision should be; they merely make it easier for such decisions to have the force of law.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Overall, there are many commonsense elements in the Women’s Charter amendments, but I feel I ought to still lay them out simply here, so that it puts my additional requests to the Minister in perspective.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, we feel that family and marriage in Singapore ought to be protected and strengthened.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This has been the case for many years and is something that most of us support.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, we should make it easy for people to get married, whether the signifier is online or not.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am also strongly supportive of allowing religious ceremonies as part of the process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For many of us who believe in matters beyond the earthy, binding ourselves to a partner has a deeply spiritual dimension.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Reminding ourselves of this, in a public, open and memorable manner is a strong commitment device.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Second, that no one goes into a marriage looking for divorce.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But having decided to do so, one should be helped along, as much as possible, by the administration of the process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In this, the amendments provide a smoothening of the path, once decisions have been made.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am not sure of the term “therapeutic justice” when referring to the amendments allowing for “divorce by mutual agreement”.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: To me, this is not about justice but about the freedoms to enter into a contract and the exit clauses which we can choose to exercise.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Whatever the name, I support this move which, I think, accords respect and dignity to both parties.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Like marriage, divorce is seldom a bloodless, contractual, dry process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am sure we all know of friends, colleagues, residents whose marriage did not work out and they decide to part ways – some on good terms, some rather acrimonious.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Whatever the case, while we cannot take the emotions out of it entirely, we can and should reduce the bureaucratic pain as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The third element, also commonsensical, is less often discussed.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: That is to say, ensure that parents, who now have to take care of separate households, will be able to do so.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We must recognise that divorce is a major life stressor for the individuals involved, permanently affecting workplace livelihoods and family structures.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Divorce proceedings should consider the livelihood concerns of single mothers and how they can be supported.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I ask for us to consider how to better support such single mothers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Both these points have, over the years, been made by NTUC and fellow labour Members.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We should review the existing Tripartite Standard for Flexible Work Arrangements or consider other support systems or policies for employers to help their employees better manage their work-life needs through flexible work options.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Work and marriage may seem quite far apart in terms of legislation but, in reality, one impacts the other.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Flexible work arrangements have suddenly come upon us in force, due to the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have seen how such work arrangements benefit so many of us, especially for working mothers, so that they can fulfil all the roles which they desire, with minimal impact on their career development.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Wearing the hat of an employer, it would be remiss of me to assume no one takes advantage of work-from-home (WFH) arrangements.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I think all of us have seen the very small minority who could be not working from home but skiving from home.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is important that we do not jettison such WFH arrangements for fear of abuse by this small minority.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We could, for example, deter such behaviour by ensuring that they are sanctioned in the same way as all HR violations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: After all, this is COVID-19 and we are already in 2022.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Women’s Charter was a document written in the 1960s at a time when the fight for equality was nascent and the problems more severe.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Today, as what Minister of State Sun Xueling has said, Singaporean women stand shoulder to shoulder with Singaporean men on many issues.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But today, as with yesterday, we still have some way to go in ensuring equal respect and eradicating violence and bias.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to consider that the support for work, with dignity and in a fulfilling job, as single parents, be written into the amendments so as to allow each one of us, women and men, to live fully whatever life choices we make.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In this debate, I wish to make a few comments on the provisions relating to divorce, in particular, the introduction of a provision allowing divorce by mutual agreement or DMA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The new section 95A will add this new fact to the existing facts for divorce which centre around adultery, unreasonable behaviour, desertion and separation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This will empower the parties to a marriage to decide for themselves whether their marriage has failed, as they are probably the best-placed parties to assess whether they can continue to maintain the marriage.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Currently, the potentially acrimonious nature of divorce proceedings can be traumatic.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To illustrate, in my past professional work, I have seen how the children of the marriage can be pressured by one parent to give evidence against the other parent in a bid to prove that the other parent was an unreasonable or irresponsible person.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The scars on the family from divorce are undeniable.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If the amendment in this Bill can reduce the acrimony and emotional toll on the divorcing family, I support that rationale fully.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, the Minister of State explained in some detail how the DMA provisions will work.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, I wish to seek two clarifications about this change.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, to what extent can the parties override the traditional grounds for divorce?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The new fact of mutual agreement broadens the possibility of divorce beyond the conventional grounds.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For the conventional grounds, the law imposes time requirements which need to be satisfied.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For instance, for adultery and unreasonable behaviour, the Women's Charter has always required that the offended spouse must not have continued to live with the offending spouse for more than six months after the last incident.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This is to show that the offended spouse finds it unreasonable to continue living with such behaviour from the offending spouse.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As for the fact of desertion, the offending spouse must have abandoned the other party for a continuous period of two years or more.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As for using separation as a fact of divorce, the period required is that either of the spouses have lived apart for at least four years, or for at least three years where the other spouse consents to the divorce.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: With the introduction of DMA, it seems to me that parties can agree to divorce where the situations could have come under the traditional grounds but the usual timeframes have not been met.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To this end, I wonder if retaining the provision for divorce on three years' separation with consent makes sense, as it may be redundant to insist on three years once the parties have agreed to divorce.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Since the purpose of allowing mutual agreement is to do away with onerous requirements of the traditional grounds, the parties can override what was required previously and set their own personal threshold for concluding that their marriage has failed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is there a risk then that divorce would become too easy?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On this question, I do note that there is no change to the requirement that one cannot, generally, file for divorce until after three years of marriage.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I agree that this requirement should be preserved.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, with the introduction of DMA, the requirements for divorce have arguably been relaxed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Should we then expect an increase in divorce rates?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second clarification on DMA is how the rights of the spouses and children will be safeguarded.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The proposed section 95(6) provides that the spouses must enter any agreement with certain requirements which include spelling out what considerations they have given to sorting out their financial affairs and any child of the marriage.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am concerned about the risk that the parties may enter into an agreement which is unfair to one spouse or not in the best interest of the children.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This could well happen when the spouses have unequal bargaining power or when one spouse has legal representation and the other does not.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In my view, it is critical for the Court to play a watchdog role for any vulnerable parties.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As Members of Parliament, we do come across single parents who are frustrated and demoralised by having to file repeated applications to Court to get ex-spouses to pay up.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These efforts incur legal costs and may require multiple Court attendances without any tangible outcome.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I also understand that when there are arrears in maintenance payments, it is not uncommon that the defaulting parent will be allowed to pay the arrears in instalments, placing further hardship on the other parent to find ways to pay bills and feed the children.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I look forward to studying the upcoming changes, which, hopefully, will strengthen support for single parents and secure children's rights.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I fully support this on the basis that this might be less damaging to the emotional well-being of any children involved and goes some way towards protecting the children.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Currently, when it comes to the paying of maintenance post-divorce, the onus is usually on the man to maintain his ex-wife and children.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Over the years, the issue of gender-neutral maintenance has been raised in this House many times.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: There are more men who choose to stay at home to look after the children and the household these days.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: An in-depth study of some of these fathers found that most of them made the choice because their wives were earning more than them.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Indeed, in a double-income household, women may be earning more than their husbands.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: What happens in the case of a divorce?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But it is now 2022 and perhaps we can make further progress in moving towards gender-neutral arrangements for maintenance.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: In many countries, including the United States, Australia, Canada and many European countries, men can claim maintenance from their wives.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: In Britain, spousal maintenance is paid by the man or woman with the higher income to the one with the lower income.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: It may be timely for us to re-examine if we should further level the playing field to ensure that our maintenance laws reflect the changes in society and are fair to both parties.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, the current amendment to the Women's Charter is mainly focused on the adjustment of the divorce proceedings by adding the sixth fact as grounds for divorce to the existing five, namely, both husband and wife can mutually agree that the marriage has broken down irretrievably, or "divorce by mutual agreement", (DMA) in short.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We also understand that the Family Justice Courts has been simplifying divorce proceedings since 2015 to allow couples who want to divorce to do so after they have reached an agreement on the divorce, together with all the ancillary matters.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Many people feel that once the Bill is passed, most of the divorcing couples will file for divorce on grounds of DMA.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: With the amendment, I hope that the divorce rate here in Singapore will not increase significantly, resulting in more single-parent families.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: In China, when divorce laws were relaxed in 2003, couples can divorce without going to court.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: As a result, the divorce rate increased significantly.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: As a result, the Chinese government had to tighten the divorce laws in 2021.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Therefore, I urge that when examining the grounds for divorce filed by couples, judges do not grant a divorce easily just because both parties have agreed that their marriage has broken down irretrievably.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We hope that the judges will lean towards requiring divorcing couples to undergo counselling.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: On another note, when the Women's Charter was amended in 2016, Mr Speaker, who was then Minister for Social and Family Development, stressed that MSF would appoint maintenance officers to enforce maintenance orders more effectively.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: However, during my Meet-the-People Sessions, many single parents still fret over claiming maintenance.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Currently, single parents have to go to different agencies in person to verify their documents before they can apply to Court to enforce the maintenance order.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Therefore, I hope that MSF can further simplify the procedures, especially in light of the COVID-19 situation, to make it easier for single parents to receive maintenance from their ex-spouse.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, notwithstanding the above concerns, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This will help parties to move on with their lives and the lives of any children involved.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Where children are involved, understanding and acting in the best interests of the child are the most important things.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I do not think that the requirement to allege fault does anything to protect the sanctity of the institution of marriage or improve the lot of the child.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Having said that, there are two aspects of the Bill that are crucial to providing important safeguards in light of the proposed amendments.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: First, as described in Parts 3 and 4 of the Bill, the provisions related to pre-agreement on matters related to parenting and finances, counselling, mediation, programmes for children, family support programmes and reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: These are all very important safeguards against the criticism that the Bill makes divorce too easy.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: More importantly, it is in the best interests of the family.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Indeed, stronger processes for counselling and mediation pre-marriage as well as before and after a divorce must also go hand in hand with the current proposals in this Bill.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Second, as described in Part 5, are the broader enforcement powers granted to the Court over custody and child access orders.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Of all the foundations upon which we build our lives, family is the most important and we are moved to recognise that kids need their moms and their dads to raise them.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Society needs their moms and dads to raise them.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We have all heard of parents, men and women, who have shirked their responsibilities as parents after divorce.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But we have also heard of parents, again men and women, though notably more men, who want nothing more than to remain a core part of their child's life but are prevented from doing so.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: He now has access and a good relationship with his teenage son.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But I have other residents who are still fighting, who are alienated from their kids, where once a loving relationship existed.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: To that end, I have a few questions and suggestions for the Minister's consideration.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: One, will the Government allocate more funding and resources to counselling and mediation services to provide trained help for couples, especially vulnerable couples, during the divorce process but also prior to marriage and at the point where they face marriage difficulties, where a marriage might yet be saved?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Two, should there not be a minimum time period for the proceedings to allow proper reflection, consideration and reconciliation?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This should not prevent applications for interim support, injunctions or family violence orders, and voluntary counselling and mediation should continue as planned.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Further, has the Minister considered making it a requirement for divorcing couples to take a parenting education course – perhaps this is the MPP referred to by the Minister of State – but including information on reconciliation or to take it even further, making counselling and mediation mandatory?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Three, regardless of the grounds for divorce, should there be a minimum period – say, six months to a year – after the final judgment and orders, during which counsellors and mediators check in on the parties to ensure both parents and children are coping well and that the orders are being adhered to?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Four, there is, in some quarters, a perception that the system is biased against men and there is a limited range of support services for men.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: At this point, I want to recognise the millennial men, who, I think, take on a much more equal role in parenting than their predecessors and are often very close to their children.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: When things do not work out between the couple, they want to keep that bond.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I believe that, for the most part, all services are equally available to men and women.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But what is the Government doing to address this perception?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Five, fighting for access to their children is a costly affair that spans years for affected parents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But as my resident told me, when it comes to your child, you will fight all the way, even if it drains your finances, even if you have to represent yourself, which is sub-optimal.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Notwithstanding the provisions on enforcement of access orders, can more funds be allocated to legal aid and means tests relaxed so as to increase legal assistance to vulnerable parents?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Notwithstanding the above, I would like to thank MSF for continuing to update the Women's Charter and continuing to advocate for women and children's issues.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There are two parts of this Bill which I wish to speak on.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: First is clause 35, which talks about the enhancement of enforcement powers relating to access to a child.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In principle, I agree with the provisions of section 126A of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, I would caution that before making any order to the bailiff to seize a child, the Court should consider taking action against the parent who is in breach of the custody order.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Seizure of a child, especially if the child is of a tender age, must be done in a sensitive manner so as not to cause any emotional trauma to the child who is caught in the dispute between the parents.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also support the provisions of section 126B.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This new provision will allow an aggrieved parent legal powers to enforce his or her right of access to the child.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I believe that most matrimonial lawyers would have come across cases where one party who was granted access to his or her own child, referred to in the Bill as Party X, had faced difficulties trying to gain access to that child.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Sometimes, this is because the other parent, referred to as Party Y, feels that depriving Party X to access is a way of getting back at Party X.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And Party Y feels that by not allowing the ex-spouse to see the child, he or she is punishing Party X.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There are also cases where Party Y may threaten to prevent Party X from seeing the child unless Party X concedes to the demands of Party Y.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In other words, the child is used as a negotiating tool to compel Party X to back down.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The child should not be used as a negotiating pawn in disputes between two warring spouses.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Any parent who chooses to breach the child access order would have to face the consequences.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also support granting powers to the Court to order Parties X, Y and the child to attend compulsory counselling so that all involved parties can understand that it is in the best interest of the child to grow up with both parents who love and care for the child.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is better than having a child grow up resenting and hating an absent parent who has been deprived of access.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many matrimonial lawyers would have also come across cases where one parent tries to poison the mind of the child against the other parent by constantly saying negative things about that parent without care and control.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In such cases, providing the Court with the power to order the parents to attend educational programmes and for the child to attend therapeutic programmes or family support programmes is an option that would mitigate the toxic effect of the poisoning of the child’s mind.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I have two queries about clause 35.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In my view, where a parent in default is recalcitrant, the Court’s power to impose a fine or sentence to incarceration will serve as a strong deterrent not to disobey a Court order.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, Sir, I am mindful that there may be occasions when an older child may refuse to see the other parent due to previous negative experiences of being physically or emotionally abused.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Or that child may witness his Parent Y being abused by Parent X.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Hence, if the child grew up filled with anger against that abusive parent, he may resist any order for access granted to the parent who was abusive.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In situations like this, I hope that a judge hearing such enforcement applications will exercise discretion to interview the child or appoint a counsellor for the child to hear the child’s point of view before making any order of fine or imprisonment.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I hope that the Court will be able to discern the circumstances where an access order may not be practical due to an abusive parent.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We should not allow an abusive or vindictive parent to abuse the legal process and commit the other parent to jail.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Second, on clause 35, may I ask the Minister of State whether we have enough counsellors to help divorcing parents deal with the issue of access?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When the Family Courts introduced the compulsory Mandatory Parenting Programme (MPP), I thought that MPP would have counsellors who can help couples think through the process before applying for divorce.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, I was told that MPP is a short session to advise the applicant on the need to make provisions for the child of the marriage.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am certainly glad to hear the Minister of State say that MPP would be enhanced to provide more support to couples thinking of divorce.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This new section provides a new ground for parties to apply for a divorce if Parties X and Y agree that the marriage has broken down irretrievably – what is described by MSF as divorce by mutual agreement, or DMA.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In 2016, the then Minister for Social and Family Development summed up the Government's policy as follows: “Singapore is our home for family.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Strong families are, and must remain, the basic building blocks of our society.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the coming years, my Ministry will continue to strengthen fundamental family relationships and support vulnerable families.” Sir, if you find this familiar, this speech was made by you when you were then the Minister for Social and Family Development.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: My understanding of a family in Singapore is that it constitutes a married couple with children and they form the usual family structure in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, if the Government's policy is to have strong families which are the building blocks of society, then I submit that the Government must do more to promote the institution of marriage so as to strengthen the parties’ commitment to marriage.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: A marriage is a serious commitment by two parties to enter into a union with each other.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In most marriage vows, each party will, minimally, undertake or pledge to the other that they will love, comfort, honour the other party in sickness and in health so long as they both shall live.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
