text: For example, when the most recent round of property cooling measures was introduced by MND, there emerged some online chatter advising and encouraging couples seeking to own multiple properties to decouple and divorce in name just to avoid the Additional Buyers' Stamp Duties!

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Important issues have been raised by Members regarding the proposals and the very institutions of marriage and family in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Marriage is the cornerstone of family formation in our society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We must protect the institution of marriage by ensuring the significance of the solemnisation and registration of marriages and that marriages contracted here are genuine.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our first priority is to save marriages where possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where there is no alternative but divorce, our aim is to help families heal and move on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Reducing acrimony and promoting child-centricity in divorce are key.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Women's Charter is a significant Act, enacted in 1961.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Women’s Charter sets out how family and family relationships should be managed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To quote Prof Leong Wai Kum, School of Law, SUSS, "the Women's Charter promulgated the idea of marriage as an equal cooperative partnership of different efforts".

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Women's Charter also provides for protection of women and girls in the areas of vice, prostitution activities for which there is good reason for this distinction as women are disproportionately affected.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And while Singapore women today are better educated with better employment opportunities, there are still vulnerable women who require the protection of the Women's Charter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Moving on to the issues regarding the marriage-related proposals, in reviewing the marriage processes under the Women's Charter, we sought to achieve two key things.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The amendments will enable us to take the marriage process online via the "Our Marriage Journey" portal later this year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh raised concerns of marriages of convenience, and I assure Members that the Registry of Marriages will continue to perform due diligence.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If there are concerns, the declaration would be performed in-person or via video-link, instead of online, and the Registrar may decide not to permit solemnisation via video-link.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how many marriages of convenience we have seen and how many have been involved in vice activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not track if they have engaged in vice activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked if the digital certificates would apply to both civil and religious ceremonies and who would issue the digital certificates.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Digital certificates would apply to all solemnisations and will be issued by the Registrar of Marriages.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling voiced concerns that digitalising the solemnisation may downplay its significance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Hence, couples may choose to hold their solemnisation in-person.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, we have seen that most couples still prefer to hold their solemnisations in-person.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, while a digital marriage certificate will be issued, a hardcopy ceremonial marriage certificate will also be provided as a keepsake.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Through the "Our Marriage Journey" portal, we will continue to emphasise the importance of the solemnisation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Second, we sought to update the necessary safeguards to ensure that the institution of marriage is not abused and continues to be protected.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Beyond legislative amendments, upcoming initiatives also boost our efforts to strengthen marriages and families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have brought together stakeholders, community partners and Singaporeans to co-create and implement solutions through the launch of the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships last year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also woven support for couples into the marriage process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested more can be done to encourage couples to attend marriage preparation courses, including by making it mandatory.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The "Our Marriage Journey" portal will recommend and encourage couples to sign up for such courses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, it is only mandatory where one party is below the age of 21, as the dissolution rates for such marriages are relatively higher.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also agree with Ms Joan Pereira that it is important that solemnisers are equipped with counselling skills.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have started a pilot initiative, Journey with You, referred to as JOY, in short, which enables licensed solemnisers to mentor newlyweds in the first year of marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will undergo training and are provided referral resources.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I am glad that there is consensus among Members on several areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First, as raised by many Members, divorce is and must be a last resort.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where possible, we aim to save the marriage and help couples resolve their issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that couples should be encouraged to seek counselling early, before marital issues worsen.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where there is no other option apart from divorce, we aim to help couples to heal, and we also ensure that the welfare of the children is protected.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong brought up the worrying trend of more recent cohorts divorcing earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: He asked why such a trend has emerged.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We believe that this is due, in part, to higher expectations of marital satisfaction and greater stressors in the early years of marriage, especially as more couples are dual income and they juggle career and parenthood.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is a trend not just emerging in Singapore but it has been apparent in many parts of the world for some time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Therefore, as raised by Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, our commitment is to protect the marriage and save it where possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The legislative amendments must be seen in totality with non-legislative initiatives which will help couples resolve issues at all stages of their relationship.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When stresses begin to emerge, we have marital and family counselling under the FAM@FSC to help families resolve issues early.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested that marriage therapy be made more accessible and affordable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked if there are sufficient trained professionals to cater to demand, what the average waiting time is for appointments and if there is remedial action if the couple do not attend subsequent counselling sessions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar similarly asked about funding and resources for such services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In terms of waiting time, parties will be contacted by the agency within a week.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As these counselling sessions are voluntary, there is no remedial action that can be taken by the Ministry or FAM@FSC should the couple not choose to continue.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, if counselling is ordered by the Court, then, in the case of non-compliance, the Court may make any further orders as it deems fit, including staying proceedings until parties have attended counselling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If couples are not able to resolve their issues and are contemplating divorce, we are also working on a Family Assist portal which will provide couples with links to marital counselling and allow reflection and also information so that couples can make an informed decision.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng had asked if the Ministry will consider mandating pre-divorce counselling for couples citing DMA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar raised similar points on requiring divorcing couples to take parenting education courses and making counselling mandatory.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At MPP, counsellors may assess the couple's suitability for reconciliation and refer them for further support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will explore extending pre-divorce counselling further at a later stage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also fully agree with Dr Shahira Abdullah that religious organisations can play an important role in mediation and counselling and parties may choose to opt for counselling by religious organisations if they are of the same faith.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, it is through learning from the Syariah Court's positive experience that we have decided to introduce pre-divorce counselling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members also agree that it is key that families are supported throughout the divorce process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the Programme for Children, Ms Joan Pereira raised the importance to support all children, including the older ones.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We fully agree and, as part of MPP, the counsellor would encourage parents to sign their children up for suitable programmes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To Mr Louis Ng and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's queries on why the Programme for Children is not mandatory, what the types of interventions under the Programme for Children are and whether there can be a national body to harmonise programmes for all children affected by Muslim and civil divorce, I would first like to assure Members, such as Dr Shahira Abdullah, who also brought up the need for Muslim marriages to be supported, that MSF and MCCY work closely together to ensure that the programmes offered to all children affected by divorce are similar.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, the Programme for Children is also available to children affected by Muslim divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is, therefore, no need for a separate body to oversee this.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Programme for Children covers various component items.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It includes an assessment of the needs of the child, counselling, psychological services as well as specific evidence-based programmes, such as Children-in-Between.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are also mindful that mandating counselling for all children may also cause additional stress and that not all children may be ready for the programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Lastly, on the issue of child access enforcement, I agree with Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim that children should not be used as a negotiating tool in their parents' quarrels and those who breach access orders must face consequences.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Court may reverse the grant of care and control to the access parent if it is in the best interest of the child to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On orders to make-up access, as with all orders related to the child, the Court will make this order taking into consideration the best interest of the child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For parties with counselling orders, FAM@FSCs and DSSAs will work closely with the Courts to support them on issues faced with access.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The 10 FAM@FSCs set up by the end of this year will be able to manage the expected caseload.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, we have also heard different views raised by Members, particularly on whether we should make the divorce process more expeditious or whether doing so could lead to easier divorces and erode the institution of marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I fully agree with Ms Sylvia Lim, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Melvin Yong that a balance must be struck between making it too difficult for couples to divorce and making it too easy to give up their commitment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Beyond non-legislative efforts to strengthen the family and upstream measures to help families facing stress, we also want to ensure that the divorce process affords parties opportunities to save their marriage and u-turn on their decision, and that the divorce process, even with the introduction of DMA, is not made easier nor faster.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The divorce process also remains largely the same no matter which fact is cited, including DMA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The three-year minimum period is an important safeguard to ensure that couples do not enter or exit a marriage lightly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The first year of marriage is often not an easy one, given the many transitions and adjustments for couples.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The three-year minimum period will, thus, allow couples sufficient time to adjust, seek help and overcome difficulties, rather than simply leave the marriage just because things are difficult.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If they truly wish to pursue divorce, the three-year minimum period will also allow them sufficient time to consider their decision carefully and also make attempts at reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, where there are legitimate reasons where a party may need to exit the marriage before the three-year minimum marriage period is up, the Women's Charter allows for that.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, where parties have made and failed at every effort to save their marriage and have no other option left but divorce, then there is a need and a place for DMA, in cases where parties agree on the divorce, to reduce acrimony.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked why DMA is needed when the separation fact allows couples to divorce without apportioning fault.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Divorcees who have filed for divorce on the simplified divorce track have shared with us in our engagements that though they had agreed on the divorce and ancillary matters, having to cite a fault-based fact did dredge up pain and hurt and the hurt deepened when parties read the affidavits from each other.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They expressed how they wanted instead to be able to take joint responsibility for the marital breakdown instead of citing fault.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They also told us that they found it difficult to rely on the separation fact as they felt that their lives were put on hold during the separation period and they could not move on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It was also not good for their children's well-being because, try as they might, they admitted they could not focus on their children until the divorce was finalised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the meantime, the children were exposed to the tensions in their relationship during the separation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: DMA, therefore, allows such couples to jointly take responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage and heal and to move on from the divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan raised concerns as to whether DMA would effectively reduce acrimony, given parties must submit the reasons leading them to conclude the marriage has irretrievably broken down and they may disagree on matters concerning their children and finances.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is inevitable that, in certain cases, even with DMA, the couple will still face acrimony in the divorce process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, providing the option for parties to jointly take responsibility rather than pinning the blame solely on one party would more likely set the frame and mindset for a less acrimonious and conflictual process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Thereafter, when parties proceed to the ancillary discussion, they are more likely to do so without the resentment of either having to bear full blame for the divorce or the pain of having to dredge up past hurts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Having jointly taken responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage, they can begin ancillary discussions more amicably.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some jurisdictions have removed the ability for a party to contest the proceedings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Spikes or long-term increase in divorce rates occur when the regime switches from fault-based to non-fault-based.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We had made this transition in 1980 from a purely fault-based regime to a hybrid regime with no-fault grounds and we had introduced a Simplified Divorce Track in 2015.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We saw no significant increase in divorce then.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members also raised queries on the divorce-related proposals.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In fact, as Dr Shahira Abdullah has pointed out, one of the aims of DMA is to spare children the pain of having their parents make, prove and disprove allegations against each other’s misdeeds, so children are better able to cope with the divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked how the Court would assess if a marriage is still reconcilable and whether MSF would be able to make recommendations to the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng similarly asked if the assessment would involve professionals in family matters.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Sylvia Lim expressed concerns about whether DMA would lower the threshold for divorce, compared to the other five facts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ultimately, the legal test for the granting of the divorce is the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are, currently, five facts with their own respective requirements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: DMA is a broad ground, but parties will still have to meet the threshold of irretrievable breakdown of marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If parties cite evidence relating to one of the five established facts, but do not quite meet the prescribed requirements, it remains open to the Court to grant the divorce on the grounds of DMA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But before doing so, the Court will have to assess the facts carefully, bearing in mind that a divorce cannot be granted under DMA if there is a reasonable possibility of reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Court will have to carefully consider whether or not to depart from the requirements of one of the five established facts, taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Court will have to assess the agreement based on the matters set out in the statement of particulars submitted by parties to the Court, which contains the three requirements needed by DMA, and make an assessment that the efforts detailed suffice to satisfy the parties-centric test that parties have made best efforts and have done all things necessary to attempt reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is not present in the current five facts, including forced separation with or without consent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All these represent a paradigm shift that is different from, but not necessarily easier than, the current five facts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Over time, the Courts will develop case law on DMA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A party who relies on DMA will thus not necessarily be able to obtain a divorce sooner than a party who relies on adultery, desertion or unreasonable behaviour.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For couples with minor children, they will have to attend MPP at the DSSA or FAM@FSC before filing for divorce or filing a counterclaim when served with divorce papers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will enhance MPP to encourage couples to consider reconciliation, if possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For couples who are open to reconciliation, a counsellor can help to support them through this process and, otherwise, the couple may proceed to divorce should they wish to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the point of filing, should the Court assess that reconciliation is still a reasonable possibility, the Court may refer the couple for counselling at DSSA or FAM@FSC.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: After counselling, parties may continue with the divorce process should they choose to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Joan Pereira similarly raised concerns on the submission of efforts to reconcile to the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In particular, Ms Pereira was concerned that this would add tension to an already strained relationship.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The premise of DMA is to allow divorcing couples to come together and help a broken relationship without further strain.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We expect that couples who cite DMA would have discussed their issues and how to resolve the dissolution of the marriage in an amicable manner.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is for this reason that the fact is founded on mutual agreement.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If there is no consensus on all matters, it is highly unlikely that the couple would opt for this fact.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The application, therefore, gives the couple space to discuss, communicate and resolve all issues, including reconciliation efforts, before presenting this application by mutual agreement to the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To Ms Hany Soh’s query on whether DMA may only be cited on the Simplified Track and if divorces filed citing another fact can later be allowed to proceed on an amended claim under DMA, we envisage that most parties who cite DMA would file on the Simplified Track.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, DMA is not limited only to the Simplified Track, and those on the standard track may choose to cite DMA as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As for whether parties who originally cited another fact can later be allowed to amend their claim and cite DMA, parties can apply for leave to amend the claim, subject to fulfilling the requirements of the Family Justice Rules.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about a minimum time period for the proceedings to allow for reflection.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked how long the process will take from the time divorce is filed and if the couple can appeal the Court’s decision.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The average duration taken depends on the track that the divorce application proceeds on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For couples who contest the divorce or ancillary matters, the duration varies and could take some time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We envisage that couples who cite DMA would likely file for divorce on the Simplified Track, but citing DMA instead of the existing five facts would not change the duration in any way.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As for appeals, as this is a consent application, it is unlikely that there should be an appeal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And should one party change their mind, they can apply to set aside the grant of the Interim Judgment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Regarding Ms Mariam Jaafar's suggestion for a minimum period after the divorce is finalised for counsellors to check in on couples to ensure that they are coping well, any family that has issues with the divorce or its impact can seek post-divorce support at the FAM@FSCs and DSSAs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked how the Court will ensure that the agreement under DMA is entered out of the parties' own volition.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked if the Court would act as a watchdog, in cases of vulnerable spouses who may be coerced into agreeing into a divorce under DMA and to unfavourable terms under the divorce relating to their children and their financial affairs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I have said earlier, we rely on family lawyers to prevent such cases.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, the mandatory parenting programme or MPP, which I have been referring to, is a mandatory pre-filing programme for parents and this can act as a safeguard against such instances, as the counsellor may identify and assist such spouses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members also raised queries on other aspects of the divorce process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the penalties that may be imposed on parties should they be found to have divorced for financial benefits, such as to own multiple properties without additional buyers’ stamp duties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I assure Members again that DMA does not make it easier for parties to get a divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In fact, parties who choose to go on DMA have to satisfy the Court that there is no reasonable possibility of reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Lawyers must also do their part to ensure that divorces are genuine and their clients are not intending to enter into a divorce just in name.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked where one party refuses to attend MPP, whether the other party would be hindered from proceeding with the divorce, such as in cases of family violence, where the perpetrator may be unwilling to attend.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As for the perpetrator, he or she must attend the MPP if he or she wishes to file a counterclaim to put forth his or her points relating to the divorce and ancillary matters to the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: DSSAs and FAM@FSCs will also refer parties for support if they disclose experiences with family violence.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Regarding the issue of child access enforcement, I would like to assure Ms Hany Soh that should parties be ordered to take part in therapeutic programmes or counselling at the DSSAs or FAM@FSCs, they will not incur any fees.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As to increasing the number of complimentary sessions for parties to carry out supervised access at DSSAs, there are no plans to do so as the intention is to foster a sense of responsibility in parents in managing their own relationship to co-parent effectively, by requiring them to contribute a sum for supervised access.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Supervised Exchange and Supervised Visitation is intended as an interim measure to help parents work towards independent access.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would also like to assure Members that should any parent face issues of access to their children, they are able to seek help at the FAM@FSCs and DSSAs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar has pointed out, there is no difference in services offered to men and women.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As for increased legal assistance to parents, the means test is reviewed at regular intervals, every five years or so, with the last amendment to means testing done in 2019.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MinLaw will continue to review the means test regularly in order to ensure that less privileged persons who need legal help continue to get it.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Legal Aid Bureau also has a merits test in order to ensure that legal aid is not given for frivolous, unmeritorious claims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Thus, it is not just about ensuring that those who need it get legal help for access matters but that the manner in which they conduct the case and the merits of their position in the case are reasonable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For access matters, Court litigation should very much be the last resort.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Mr Lim Biow Chuan also raised concerns regarding the provision to allow the Court to direct the bailiff to restore a child to the physical custody of a person in whose custody, or care and control, the child is placed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To safeguard the child’s well-being, the bailiff will be accompanied by the applicant, usually the other parent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where required, the bailiff is also empowered to activate Auxiliary Police Officers for support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is pertinent to note that the same powers exist in the Guardianship of Infants Act and are available to all parents and guardians of a child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This proposal seeks to extend the same relief to parents who have divorce, nullity or judicial separation proceedings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the issue of maintenance enforcement, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Ang Wei Neng noted that the current maintenance enforcement process can be further enhanced.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Ang Wei Neng also raised the issue of allowing maintenance applications to be made for husbands, without the condition of incapacity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, while women are in a much better position today than they were many years ago, we recognise that, even today, in a marriage, it is more likely for a wife to give up her career to care for her family, while her husband continues working.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And this means that post-divorce, women tend to be financially more vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While we want to move towards gender-neutrality, those who are more vulnerable must be protected.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In any case, the Courts refrain from granting high amounts of maintenance to wives who are able to work, even if they had not worked or stopped working for some years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Courts' goal is to award reasonable maintenance that will meet the financial needs of the wife until she can secure for herself some form of employment and adjust to her post-divorce situation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The issue of parental alienation was also brought up by Ms Mariam Jaafar.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not think that there is a need to define the term "parental alienation" in order to ensure that those who are impacted by it are supported.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Rather, parents who believe that they are victims of parental alienation are encouraged to seek help for themselves and their children at FSCs or DSSAs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if such methods fail, parents may consider legal recourse.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We also recognise that there may be those impacted by divorce that require even more support, given the challenges of caregiving.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Seah Kian Peng brought up the issue of support for mothers who may be unemployed during the divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MPP covers several areas, including co-parenting and the impact of divorce on parties' financial status and living arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If employment support or financial support is needed, the MPP counsellor would refer the parties for employment or financial assistance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Seah Kian Peng also asked about support for parents with caregiving responsibilities, including greater flexible work support and other policies for better work-life harmony.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOM introduced the Tripartite Advisory on Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) and Tripartite Standard on FWAs in 2017 and, subsequently, the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony in 2021, which guides employers on how to offer FWAs to their employees and provides recognition to employers who do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOM will continue to work with the tripartite partners to strengthen the provision of FWAs and other work-life practices.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In August 2021, MSF also set up an Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: One of the focal areas is on "Support for Single Parents", which aims to enable single parents to better care for their children and raise their families through strengthening the ecosystem of support around them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Alliance for Action will work with community partners to strengthen support for single parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And this includes childcare, employment and socioemotional support, facilitating support networks for single parents and developing a one-stop portal to help single parents access programmes and community resources more easily.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng brought up the issue of access to HDB flats for divorcees with shared care and control of their children and made several suggestions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under current HDB policy, all individuals are only allowed to be listed in one HDB flat application.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, divorcees with shared care and control of children have an equal right to list their children in their flat application.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For cases where the ex-spouse has bought a private property after the divorce, they may still wish to list the child in a future flat application.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As such, HDB will review each case individually and will not be able to waive the mutual agreement requirement as a blanket policy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will also not require the Court order to state which parent is allowed to list the child as an "essential occupier" as orders pertaining to a child are made with the overarching principle of the child's best interest.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When determining issues pertaining to a child's welfare, the Court order focuses on rebuilding relationships and for parents to focus on the future with their children, instead of specific orders laying down conditions, such as the one referred to.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As far as possible, we want to encourage divorced parents to work through issues cooperatively and harmoniously outside of the Court system.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is especially pertinent in cases where there is shared care and control as it is not ideal for parents with shared care and control to seek or rely on Court orders to lay down all matters and details pertaining to care of their children and arrangements after divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Instead, they should be working on co-parenting cooperatively in the child's best interest.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Those awarded share and control must also, when they applied for it, truly be able to divide the care and control of the child equally and be able to cooperate to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that there may be cases where parents are unable to reach an agreement despite their best efforts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In such cases, they can approach HDB to discuss their options.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar has raised, the area of family law is an important one, one that often most impacts people and their families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is for this reason that our proposed amendments seek to strengthen therapeutic justice in the family justice system, and we are working with FJC to include monitoring standards, processes and complaints.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, the various professions involved in the process are subject to their respective codes of practice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I believe that, viewed holistically, these proposed amendments to the Women's Charter relating to marriage and divorce, will strengthen the institution of marriage and support families should they have to pursue divorce as a last resort.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With that, I thank Members for the valuable input and support for this Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I want to thank the Minister of State for her clarifications.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: It has given me much assurance of the Government's commitment to the institution of marriage.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: If I may clarify, if DMA is not accepted by the Court, the Minister of State had said that the Court can direct parties for counselling.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: However, my understanding is that counselling requires parties to agree and, if the couple refuses to attend counselling, what does that mean for the Court's directions?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Or does it mean that the parties would then have to file for divorce based on the other grounds under section 95A of the Bill?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: My experience is that most couples, by the time they come to see a lawyer, are unwilling to consider counselling.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: And it gives them great pain to have to revisit that decision; what more if the Court has to redirect them to go for counselling.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I understand from the Minister of State that it will be made compulsory for all divorcing parents with minor children.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Can I check whether this plan is also intending to extend to those whose children have already attained the age of 21 but actually suffer from mental or physical disability?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Because, currently, when you file a proposed parenting plan, it actually applies to those parents with this kind of family settings.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I still have a lingering concern in the area of enforcement of access and parental alienation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Because the lived experience of my residents is that leaving it to FSC has not addressed the issues for them.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: And, of course, the legal recourse is very expensive and long drawn-out, which is why I had also raised the question on legal aid.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: So, I hope that, at some point, MSF will assess again a framework for parental alienation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: But I have one clarification on the use of enforcement of access.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Will this apply to divorces that have already been approved, even if it is multiple years?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Parents who feel that they have not been given due access to their children right now, will they be able to now go to Court and get their orders for access approved when their kids may say that they do not want to see them because they have been conditioned by the other spouse to actually break relationships with the previous spouse?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will have to take into account the full facts of the case.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I understand where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But the starting point of the Court has to be that it is in the best interest of the child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we hope, with the current updates to how access is provided, that this would ensure more expeditious redress for parents who face issues of access.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: So, I would just like to confirm: the enforcement powers proposed will apply to divorces that have already been finalised in the past and not only to new divorces going forward.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I would just like to speak on the point in her response about allowing husbands to seek maintenance, that, currently, it is a very small number and not the norm.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In the interest of developing and uplifting women, I would like to seek the Ministry's consideration that in order to create a mainstreaming, we must start with the right signals.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And perhaps to encourage more men to take on an equal role domestically, we may need this legislative safeguard to then nudge different behaviours.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I think that this would aid the cause for women to be unburdened from an over-proportion of care responsibilities and to encourage men to take up more of a role in the home as a participating father and spouse.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, would the Minister of State like to comment on whether we can expedite the consideration of this so that we can expedite the accelerating of a different future, in mainstreaming men's equal role domestically?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are many ongoing efforts and non-legislative ones to encourage the mainstreaming of the roles of the father and the mother, like what the Member has suggested.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, MOE, in its Character Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum talks about the roles that different family members play and they encourage children and students not to have stereotyped views on what a father and mother's roles should be.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I would encourage the Member to look at these efforts holistically.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Important lessons and initiatives also have to start very young when it comes to framing the views that society has towards what the roles of fathers and mothers should be.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I would encourage the Member to look beyond legislative amendments.      .
